source.title: Backtracking Gradient Descent Method and Some Applications in Large Scale Optimisation. Part 2: Algorithms and Experiments

record.file_problem: None; the full article text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Its experiments compare optimizer validation accuracy on CIFAR-10 and discuss dropout and batch normalization in the training procedure, but do not test most versions about memorization and generalization. Optimizer comparisons provide evidence relevant to V4, with mixed outcomes across starting learning rates.
record.gate_note: Most of the paper's experiments concern finding learning rates and comparing its own backtracking methods. Those comparisons are not rows unless they directly report a tested claim object. The optimizer table reports accuracy for standard optimizers under varied starting learning rates, which bears on V4. CIFAR-10 image classification results do not test memorization of random labels, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, batch-size generalization gaps, dropout effects, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: Table 2 directly compares held-out accuracy of adaptive optimizers with SGD and momentum methods under a learning-rate sweep on CIFAR-10. This tests V4's performance comparison; matching training accuracy or measuring a train-test gap is not required for that part of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate: the authors advocate backtracking methods with theoretical convergence guarantees and automatic learning-rate selection. They claim superior validation performance, with MBT-MMT and MBT-NAG reaching 93.70% and 93.85% versus the best standard optimizer's 92.41% in Table 2, and report robust performance across CIFAR-10/100 architectures. They do not establish a train-test-gap explanation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops backtracking learning-rate procedures and evaluates optimizer validation accuracy on CIFAR-10/100; it does not use the original claim's controlled generalization-gap comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Starting learning rate changes validation accuracy substantially in Table 2; optimizer rankings vary across starting rates. Training dataset and architecture are also varied in Table 3, which reports the authors' own MBT methods.
record.problems: No training accuracy is reported alongside validation accuracy in the optimizer comparison. Results compare best validation accuracy after 200 epochs across different starting learning rates, not matched training performance or train-test gaps. No uncertainty estimates are given.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for standard optimizer results beyond the 60-row cap are omitted; the table contains additional separate entries for Adamax and the paper's MBT methods across conditions. These are in Table 2, Experiment 4. Since rows are already at the cap and the retained results demonstrate learning-rate dependence, these were not extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Equal or better adaptive-method training performance; language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching Adam to SGD. Decay-schedule tuning is not documented.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes; Table 1 measures learning rates instead.
Dropout's effect on held-out error; temporary disabling during line search is not a dropout generalization comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Accuracy after removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: All 60 numeric values match Table 2. Subjects name optimizers, not models; ResNet18 is the model. Compare each optimizer's best learning rate rather than treating equal numerical learning rates as equally tuned. Missing training accuracy leaves one clause of V4 untested, not the entire version. Nonoptimal cells remain linked as sweep evidence but cannot independently determine the tuned comparison. No uncertainty or significance tests are reported, so small differences are descriptive. Additional Adam and Adamax cells are already declared in rows_left_out; Table 3 contains only the authors' methods and supplies no further standard-versus-adaptive comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language benchmarks, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons and generalization gap.
Direct dropout intervention and comparisons with explicit regularization removed.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its association with train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring consequent test accuracy.
